units.title: narrow the held-out refusal to brief, worktree and claims, and void a measurement on contract leakage
units.commit: fix(gate): refuse a held-out contract reachable from brief, worktree or claims
units.note:
Read ADR-0103's Enforcement section before touching anything. This unit REPAIRS K01 (commit 46e08ae), it does not undo it.

THE DEFECT, measured 24 August 2026. `.github/scripts/check_heldout_isolation.py` is 24 lines and refuses UNCONDITIONALLY: `refusal_reason()` returns a refusal for any argument and `main()` always returns 2. `scripts/dispatch.py:2500-2508` refuses any `--heldout-contract` before preflight, and its help text at dispatch.py:2458-2460 says 'refused until dispatch gains real isolation'. The consequence is that no held-out contract can be supplied to any dispatch on this architecture, so no contract-beta can be measured, so EXP-142 stays BLOCKED on its precondition and units K02, K03, K04 and AS all have nothing to stand on.

WHY THIS IS A REPAIR AND NOT A RELAXATION, and you must be able to state this yourself before you write a line. ADR-0103's Enforcement specifies the boundary exactly: 'refuses a build dispatch whose brief, worktree or claims can reach the held-out contract for that unit.' K01 refused on a broader ground -- that a same-OS-user unsandboxed child can read any file in principle -- which is true, and which converted the principal's guard into a wall that blocks his own decision. Narrowing to the specified boundary is implementing the decision. It is a relaxation ONLY if you leave the residual open, which is why the second half of this unit is mandatory and not optional.

WHAT TO BUILD.
(a) Make `check_heldout_isolation.py` decide rather than assert. It takes the contract path and the dispatch's brief text, worktree root and declared claims, and refuses when the contract is inside the worktree, named or quoted in the brief, or covered by any claim. It PERMITS otherwise, and prints what it checked. `scripts/dispatch.py` calls it with the real values instead of refusing on the flag's mere presence.
(b) Add a post-build audit mode to the SAME file -- do not create a second script. It reads the child's transcript (`<uid>.out`, `<uid>.err` under `.harness/dispatch/`) and the produced diff, and reports LEAKED if the contract's path, its sha256, or any of its distinctive content lines appear. A leaked measurement is VOID, not merely flagged.
(c) For (b), REUSE `.github/scripts/check_private_corpus.py`'s existing whole-line shingle fingerprinting -- case-folded words, >=12 words and >=80 characters, SHA-256 digests. Do not write a new fingerprinter. This is already in the codebase and it is the same problem.

WHAT YOU MUST NOT DO. Do not delete the refusal path -- a contract inside the worktree must still be refused before child launch, and `tests/test_heldout_isolation.py::test_heldout_contract_refuses_before_dispatch_preflight` must keep passing in substance. Do not build a container, a second OS user or a WSL uid boundary; that is weeks of Windows work for a residual (b) already covers, and nothing here has been measured to support it. Do not print the contract's contents in any refusal or audit output -- follow `check_private_corpus.py`, which never prints a matched private path in full.

RECORD THE RESIDUAL HONESTLY, in the module docstring: a child that reads the contract and neither echoes its path nor reproduces its assertions is not detected. Tag it `[asserted]`. That sentence is load-bearing for EXP-142's write-up and must not be softened.

DONE WHEN: a dispatch whose worktree, brief or claims can reach the contract is refused with exit 2 before child launch; a dispatch that cannot reach it proceeds; the audit mode returns LEAKED on a transcript containing the contract path, its digest, or a fingerprinted line, and CLEAN otherwise; every assertion above has a test that fails if the behaviour is removed.

units.title: author a different-family held-out contract from pre-registered intent and commit its digest before dispatch
units.commit: feat(gate): author a held-out contract from a different family before the build
deps: narrow the held-out refusal to brief, worktree and claims, and void a measurement on contract leakage
units.note:
This is K02, re-specified against the narrowed K01. It cannot run until unit 1 lands, because dispatch refuses every held-out contract until then.

WHAT MUST EXIST, per ADR-0103's Decision section. The contract is derived from the SAME stated intent as the build, by a DIFFERENT model family from the builder, committed before the build dispatch, and never placed anywhere the builder or its checks can read.

CONCRETELY.
(a) The intent statement is the unit's `title` and `note` from `.harness/plan-units.json`. That is what already exists and it is pre-registered by construction -- do not invent a new intent format.
(b) Author the contract by dispatching to a family different from the one that will build, using the family selection machinery already in `scripts/dispatch.py`. The family difference must be REFUSED AT DISPATCH if violated, not merely logged. ADR-0103 names this as one of its three checks.
(c) Write the contract OUTSIDE the unit worktree and outside anything the claims cover, so unit 1's reachability check passes.
(d) Append a `measurement.registered` trajectory event with `config_hash` = the sha256 of the contract file, BEFORE the build dispatch starts. `src/consilient/events.py:286-336` already validates this event kind and requires 64 lower-case hex; `.github/scripts/check_measurement_recorded.py` already proves CI refuses a result without prior registration. Reuse both. Do not invent a new event kind and do not write the digest into a JSON side-file.

WHY THE DIGEST MATTERS MORE THAN IT LOOKS. The commitment is what stops the contract being rewritten after the artefact exists to match what the builder did -- Goodhart through the front door, which ADR-0103 names as the thing that would make beta_T measure nothing. Without a pre-committed digest, 'authored before the build' is a claim nobody can check afterwards.

WHAT YOU MUST NOT DO. Do not let the caller supply the family of either side -- derive the builder's family from the dispatch that will actually run. Do not weaken the refusal in unit 1 to make placement convenient; move the file instead. Do not have the contract-authoring dispatch see the artefact, the builder's brief beyond the intent text, or the repository's own test suite for the claimed paths.

WATCH FOR THE TRIPWIRE, and record it: a contract that never marks a violation is not evidence of quality, it is evidence the contract was written to match what the builder was going to do anyway. The violation rate must be recorded alongside every contract so EXP-142 can report it.

DONE WHEN: a build dispatch for a measured unit refuses unless a contract digest is already in the trajectory and the authoring family differs from the builder's; the contract file sits outside the worktree and outside the claims; and a test fails if either refusal is removed.

units.title: admit contract_beta as a gate estimand, strictly separate from human-beta and from every proxy
units.commit: feat(beta): admit contract-beta for the gate, refusing every proxy estimand
deps: author a different-family held-out contract from pre-registered intent and commit its digest before dispatch
units.note:
This is K03, re-specified. It deps on AT only because AT already claims `src/consilient/projection.py` and claims are locks -- there is no logical dependency between signed verdicts and contract-beta, and the two code regions do not overlap.

WHAT EXISTS TODAY, measured 24 August 2026. `src/consilient/beta.py:39-47` defines `HUMAN_VERDICT_BETA = 'human_verdict_beta'` and `PROXY_ESTIMAND_KINDS = {mutation_proxy_beta, critic_proxy_beta, repository_consequence_false_shipment_cohort_lower_bound}`. `admits_human_beta_row` (beta.py:183-191) refuses every proxy and requires `auth_status == 'authenticated'`. `projection.py:66-67, 979, 1030-1034, 1141-1145` writes `estimand_kind` and `auth_status` onto outcome rows, and hardcodes `'human_verdict_beta'` at both write sites. Nothing anywhere writes or reads a contract-beta row. Grep for `contract_beta` across src, tests, docs, scripts and .github returns only ADR-0103 and EXP-142 prose.

WHAT TO BUILD.
(a) A `CONTRACT_BETA = 'contract_beta'` estimand kind and an `admits_gate_row()` that admits it and NOTHING else. It must refuse every kind in `PROXY_ESTIMAND_KINDS`, refuse `human_verdict_beta`, and refuse any row whose `auth_status` is not authenticated.
(b) `admits_human_beta_row` must be left EXACTLY as it is. The two admission rules stay separate functions with separate tests. ADR-0103 is explicit: human-beta is alignment, reported separately, never blocking, and its rule is 'unchanged and continues to refuse every proxy'.
(c) A projection write path that records a contract-beta outcome row: the held-out contract's verdict (violation or not) as the condition, and the project's own checks' verdict (accept or reject) as the outcome. beta_T = P(checks accept | contract violated). The row must carry the repository it was measured on, because A1 reports per repository and pooling is forbidden.
(d) A row whose measurement was marked LEAKED by unit 1's audit must be REFUSED here, not silently included.

WHAT YOU MUST NOT DO, and this is the whole point of the separation. Do not widen `PROXY_ESTIMAND_KINDS` and do not admit anything in it into the gate projection. `critic_proxy_beta`, `mutation_proxy_beta` and the repository-consequence lower bound are DIFFERENT ESTIMANDS, not cheaper estimates of the same one -- ADR-0080's algebra is that they 'say nothing about H without labels'. Do not perform the substitution `q_upper := beta_upper` that ADR-0080 forbids. Do not admit a `declared_principal` auth status: `scripts/verdict.py` lets its caller choose the principal, so a local agent process can forge one, and admitting it would let the system fabricate the ground truth used to measure its own error rate.

Do not lower `MIN_REJECTIONS` or add a knob that can lower a floor. beta.py:216-219 already refuses a `min_rejections` below the constant; contract-beta needs its own floor with the same property -- raisable only.

DONE WHEN: `admits_gate_row` admits a clean contract_beta row and refuses each of the four other kinds by name in a test; a leaked row is refused; `admits_human_beta_row`'s behaviour is byte-for-byte unchanged and a test proves it; and a Wilson interval is computed per repository with no pooling path available.

units.title: gate A1 on contract-beta over two repositories, read from the trajectory rather than a prose regex
units.commit: feat(gate): A1 reads contract-beta from the trajectory, not the retired EXP-01 route
deps: admit contract_beta as a gate estimand, strictly separate from human-beta and from every proxy
units.note:
This supersedes BOTH unit AS and unit K04, which are near-duplicates claiming `src/consilient/cli.py` for the same change on different dep chains. Retire whichever survives; do not run both.

THE DEFECT, measured 24 August 2026. `src/consilient/cli.py:426-484` computes A1 from one input: EXP-01's entry in `docs/10-research/experiment-register.md`. `EXP01_BETA` (cli.py:94-96) matches `beta-measured: p [lo, hi]`; cli.py:433-452 sets `stopping_rule_fired` from the literal string 'stopping rule FIRED' and hard-fails. EXP-01's header (experiment-register.md:45) carries that exact string, because its stopping rule fired on 20 August 2026 when the interval would not narrow below +/-0.05 and history mining was retired. `consil doctor --json` in this tree reports A1 fail with that reason. So the gate enforces a route the project itself falsified, and it is structurally unpassable: no evidence any experiment could produce opens it.

ADR-0103 is the principal's own decision, dated 23 August 2026, and it moved the gate quantity to contract-beta (beta_T). The decision moved and the code did not follow. Implement his decision; do not invent one.

WHAT TO BUILD.
(a) A1 reads the contract-beta projection from the TRAJECTORY via `admits_gate_row`, not a regex over markdown. Delete the `EXP01_BETA` route from A1 entirely.
(b) A1 requires TWO repositories, each with its own interval, never pooled. The current code has NEVER checked this: cli.py:169 says 'two differently verified repositories' and the implementation checks one regex hit in one file. Fix the mismatch rather than preserving it. The second repository must be PUBLIC -- EXP-01's corpora were the two private repositories, whose names, contents and aggregate measured metrics may not be published (AGENTS.md, Joe 23 August 2026), so no measurement on them can ever be reported. `.harness/allowed-cwds.json` already lists `itsdangerous` and `pytest-upstream`, and EXP-96 pinned Pallets `itsdangerous` 2.2.0 as an independently-verified second corpus under ADR-0013.
(c) Update the A1 requirement string at cli.py:169 to name beta_T. Take the wording from ADR-0103's Decision section; do not compose your own. This is implementing the principal's recorded decision, not changing a gate.
(d) A1 must REFUSE TO PASS while ADR-0103's status is PROVISIONAL and EXP-142 has not reported. Read the status from the ADR file. This is a sharpening, not a hurdle: ADR-0103 could still be killed if EXP-142 finds the held-out suite's errors correlated with the checks', in which case beta_T is biased downward and a gate opening on it opens on a flattering number.
(e) Human-beta is reported SEPARATELY and blocks nothing. ADR-0103's reasoning is the principal's own and must be preserved: he is by design a weaker judge of the system's output than the system, so a gate resting on his verdicts measures agreement with the weaker judge rather than correctness.

THE PROSE-EDIT HOLE, which you must close and not reproduce. `tests/test_v0_invariants.py:2871-2885` proves A1 currently reports PASS if someone edits the register to drop 'stopping rule FIRED' while keeping a `beta-measured:` line. EXP-01's own entry says so at experiment-register.md:56-58: 'this flips doctor's A1 to PASS ... One git revert returns A1 to FAIL.' A gate whose sole discriminator is a regex over a hand-editable markdown file has beta = 1 against a prose edit. Contract-beta must therefore be read from `measurement.result` events with their pre-registered `config_hash`, which `src/consilient/events.py:286-336` already validates. Delete the three EXP-01-pinned A1 tests at test_v0_invariants.py:2835-2885 and replace them with tests against the new source; leaving them would re-pin the retired route.

WHAT YOU MUST NOT DO. Do not invent a new gate condition. Do not relax or widen the interval requirement -- half-width <= 0.05 stands. Do not admit a proxy estimand; `PROXY_ESTIMAND_KINDS` exists precisely to keep `critic_proxy_beta`, `mutation_proxy_beta` and the repository-consequence lower bound out of the projection, and that separation stands. Do not make A1 depend on human-beta. Do not make it pass. ADR-0103's Enforcement section says in terms: 'none of these exists today ... Gate A1 must continue to report FAIL. That is stated here so nobody reads this ADR as having opened it.'

DONE WHEN: A1 reports FAIL with a reason naming the ABSENT contract-beta measurement rather than the retired EXP-01 route; a test fails if A1 ever passes without an interval; a test fails if A1 passes on a proxy estimand; a test fails if A1 passes on one repository; a test fails if A1 passes while ADR-0103 is PROVISIONAL; and no A1 code path reads `docs/10-research/experiment-register.md`.

condition: A2 — Replay reproduces an identical canonical state digest

units.title: Make the canonical state digest independent of where the log lives
units.commit: fix(projection): digest the log's content, not its absolute path
units.note:
THE DEFECT. Gate A2 fails deterministically on this repository, and the state does not diverge. `state_digest` (src/consilient/projection.py:1544) hashes every column of every table, and `rejections.path` (written by `_apply_rejections`, src/consilient/projection.py:279, insert at :291) holds the ABSOLUTE filesystem path of the file a refused line came from — `events.Rejection.path`, src/consilient/events.py:337, populated by `read_all` at :2852. Unit AN's pinned-prefix comparison (landed as 7e9bd0e) must rebuild the prefix in a scratch directory, `db.parent / (db.stem + "-a2-prefix")` at src/consilient/cli.py:321, so every rejection row it produces carries a different path from the persisted one. Any log with at least one refused line therefore reports 'canonical state diverged' forever. This one has six permanent ones (2026-08-20.jsonl lines 62/63/66 baselined by ADR-0043; 2026-08-22.jsonl lines 27/35/45).

THE EVIDENCE. [measured] 24 August 2026, on a frozen copy of `.harness/state.db` (2945 events) and `.harness/log`, reproducing `cmd_replay`'s comparison exactly: persisted digest `58da482c07c766…`, pinned-prefix digest `b6f2804443ef26…`. A per-table digest of both databases: every table identical EXCEPT `rejections`, 6 rows on each side, identical `id`, `line` and `reason` on all six, differing only in `path`. Rewrite `rejections.path` to its basename on both sides, re-digest, and both give `d9438ac950072222…`. A2 passes on this history the moment the path is normalised. Reproduce this before you change anything; if your reproduction disagrees, stop and report rather than proceeding.

WHAT TO DO. Two changes, both small.

1. Store the log-relative name, not the absolute path. In `_apply_rejections`, normalise the value written to `rejections.path` to the daily file's name (the log directory is flat — `read_all` and `_copy_event_prefix` both use `glob("*.jsonl")`). Do NOT change `Rejection.path` itself: it is returned out of `read_all` and used by the dashboard and by `cmd_replay`'s `quarantined` payload, where the full path is wanted. Normalise only at the database boundary. Nothing reads `rejections.path` back out of the database — verify that yourself before you rely on it.

2. Stamp the projection so the one-off change is not misreported as divergence. Adding (1) changes the digest, so the FIRST run after this lands would compare an old-code database against a new-code rebuild and report 'canonical state diverged' — a false failure on the very gate that exists to catch false verdicts, and the same false failure will recur on every future change to `SCHEMA`, `_apply` or `state_digest`. So: add a module constant `PROJECTION_VERSION` in projection.py, bump it in this commit, write it with `PRAGMA user_version = …` in `build` (sqlite has this built in — do NOT add a table; a new table would itself be covered by `state_digest`), read it from the existing database in `cmd_replay` before digesting, and when it differs from the code's constant have `_replay_condition` return status `unknown` with a reason naming both versions. This is the version half of unit AC, which is NOT in HEAD (`git merge-base --is-ancestor c91aa66 HEAD` fails); whoever lands AC later must merge with this rather than revert it.

WHAT MUST NOT BE DONE. Do not touch the prefix pinning — AN is correct and is the reason A2 is decidable at all while the log is being written. Do not widen what counts as identical, do not drop `rejections.path` from the digest (a rejection moving files must still change it), and do not make the version stamp an escape hatch: `PROJECTION_VERSION` is a constant in code, never derived from data or from the database being read, and a version MISMATCH yields `unknown`, never `pass`. A genuine mismatch inside the prefix under the SAME version must still FAIL. Do not reintroduce the tautological pass repaired on 20 August 2026: an empty prefix stays `unknown`. Do not touch `_object_status` (src/consilient/projection.py:1149) — its working-tree dependence is a real latent defect of the same shape, but it is measured NOT to be the cause here (prefix digests with `workspace=REPO` and `workspace=None` are both `b6f2804443ef26…`, and `record_facts` is empty) and it belongs to its own unit.

HOW YOU KNOW YOU ARE FINISHED. (a) tests/test_doctor_a2_concurrent.py gains a case that puts an UNREADABLE line in the log — this is the hole that let the defect through, since none of its five existing tests ever produces a rejection — and asserts A2 is `pass` with the prefix comparison intact. (b) A case asserting a same-version genuine divergence inside the prefix still returns `fail`, and (c) a case asserting a version mismatch returns `unknown`, not `pass` and not `fail`. (d) Run `consil doctor` in this worktree twice in succession: the first run may report A2 `unknown` for the version change, the second must report `pass` with a reason naming 2945-or-more compared events. Report the actual output of both runs; do not claim the gate moved without pasting what doctor said.

condition: A3 — "Seven consecutive days of trajectory capture with no data loss"
question: Do you accept baselining the three torn lines of 2026-08-22 (log lines 27, 35, 45) as a known permanent capture loss under a new ADR-0105 — raising A3's tolerated total from three lines to six — and will you record it in the trajectory as a `decision.gate_amendment` the way you did for ADR-0043 on 20 August?

units.title: Baseline the 22 August capture loss under its own pinned ratchet, not ADR-0043's
units.commit: docs(adr): baseline the 22 August capture loss under its own ratchet
units.note:
THE DEFECT, MEASURED 24 August 2026. `_capture_condition` (src/consilient/cli.py:680) passes only on `run >= 7 and new_refused == 0 and stale == 0`. `run_start` (cli.py:647-654) walks BACKWARDS through consecutive capture days, so while capture is unbroken it stays pinned at 2026-08-19 and the window never slides forward. Three lines in `.harness/log/2026-08-22.jsonl` -- lines 27, 35 and 45, digests 305cfe4853e3d9576fd186f86cac2f3900805c44a75a41b0642a27e1da5741d3, 3769e62caa9131bb916fef24b40d46d70b49e19ee59a0686aa106b66eed15387, 6511adf8d1b5ef4aea3f542d610d261572c6a103d630775ce785ab2395a187ec -- are invalid JSON and sit inside that window permanently. Today: `run` 6/7, `new_refused` 3. The only way the current code passes is a capture gap AFTER the 22nd, i.e. stop capturing for a day. A capture gate you pass by breaking capture.

STOP HERE UNLESS THE PRINCIPAL'S DECISION IS RECORDED. ADR-0043's amendment is in the trajectory as `decision.gate_amendment` authored by `joe-brown` at `.harness/log/2026-08-20.jsonl` line 70, and ADR-0043's own Enforcement says the check ships in the same commit as acceptance or not at all. There is NO `decision.*` or `human_decision` event in 2026-08-23.jsonl or 2026-08-24.jsonl. [measured] So: write the ADR at status PROPOSED, regenerate the index, and STOP. Do not touch cli.py and do not write the new test until a `decision.gate_amendment` event naming ADR-0105 and authored by `joe-brown` exists in the log. You cannot author it -- `validate()` refuses a decision attributed to the principal by anyone else, which is what the three 20 August V0-18 refusals were. If it is absent, finish with the ADR and index alone and say plainly that the code half is withheld pending the principal.

DO NOT ADD THE DIGESTS TO `HISTORICAL_REFUSAL_DIGESTS`. The earlier draft of this brief said to, and it is wrong. That set is guarded by `tests/test_v0_invariants.py:2985` (`len(...) == 3`), `:3008` (`a3_digests == set(...)`, the 2026-08-20 subset), and `:2405` (`CAPTURE_REFUSAL_BASELINE <= 3`, docstring: "the A3 refusal tolerance was raised; ADR-0043 permits it to fall only"). Relaxing any of those to make A3 pass is forbidden outright. Do not edit `tests/test_v0_invariants.py` at all -- it is not in your claim set.

WHAT TO BUILD INSTEAD, once the decision exists. Add a SECOND, separately named constant in `src/consilient/cli.py` beside the existing one -- e.g. `CAPTURE_LOSS_DIGESTS: frozenset[str]` holding exactly those three digests, with a comment naming the incident, the date and the commit that fixed the cause. Change the membership test at cli.py:626-631 to count a rejection as baseline if its digest is in EITHER set, and extend the reason string so `doctor` names both incidents separately -- ADR-0043's three V0-18 refusals and ADR-0105's three torn-append losses. Six tolerated lines reported as six, never as one opaque number. Leave `CAPTURE_REFUSAL_BASELINE` at 3. Leave the `run >= 7` arithmetic, `stale`, and the backwards walk exactly as they are: the condition is right, the history under it is damaged.

THE NEW TEST, `tests/test_doctor_a3_baseline.py`, ships in the same commit (working principle 3). It must (a) derive the 2026-08-22 rejection digests FROM THE LOG via `events.read` and assert they equal `CAPTURE_LOSS_DIGESTS` exactly -- pin against the artefact, never against a second hand-written constant, which is the drift `tests/test_v0_invariants.py:2976-2981` records; (b) assert `len(CAPTURE_LOSS_DIGESTS) <= 3`, its own ratchet, so this set cannot grow silently the way ADR-0043's was warned it might; (c) assert that a fabricated NEW rejection inside the window still fails A3, so the baseline cannot be mistaken for a removal; (d) skip cleanly when `.harness/log/2026-08-22.jsonl` is absent from the checkout.

THE ADR MUST GET THE CAUSE RIGHT. Two claims in the earlier draft are false and must not be repeated. FIRST: these lines did NOT bypass `append()`. `events.bypassed()` (events.py:2969-2998) is a canonical-form proxy that reports any invalid-JSON line as a bypass; `tests/test_v0_invariants.py:1082-1084` already records that the three "did use `append()`". SECOND: unit AB is NOT the fix. AB landed as 220e372 (ancestor of HEAD) and its guard (events.py:2838-2842) refuses an append when the file does not end with `\n` -- a TRAILING torn line. These three are INTERIOR, with valid lines after them and the file ending cleanly; AB would have caught none of them. The real mechanism is a lost-update race between two unlocked concurrent writers that computed the same end-of-file offset: line 26 is 1193 bytes + newline = 1194, the intact `capability.gap` for a 9179-byte `dispatch.outcome` is 9061 + newline = 9062, and 9062 - 1194 = 7868 = line 27's 7867 surviving bytes plus its newline. [algebra over measured bytes] The cure is 3d8461f "feat(events): make ordinary append durable and process-serialised", 2026-08-22 22:33:13 +0100 -- nine hours after the last tear at 12:33:54Z -- which holds an exclusive per-file lock across `lseek(SEEK_END)`, write and fsync in `_write_validated` (events.py:2393-2408), extended to `_transaction` by 15d72ce. Cite 3d8461f as the fix and AB as separate hardening of a different tear mode.

EVIDENCE THE CAUSE IS CLOSED, for the ADR's Enforcement section -- it already exists, do not build a new one: `tests/test_event_durability.py:70` spawns 10 processes × 20 appends and asserts 200 valid distinct lines with no rejections; and 2026-08-23 (938 events) and 2026-08-24 (1339 events) carry zero rejections and zero misdated lines under a many-process build loop. [measured]

EVIDENCE AGAINST -- write these, do not soften them. (1) A3's tolerated total rises from three lines to six. That is a gate boundary moving on the initiative of the party it binds, for the second time, and ADR-0043's own "What would overturn this" anticipated exactly this: it said the ratchet is decorative if the count has not FALLEN in three months. It has risen. Say so. (2) The bound on this is not a judgement a test can make. No check can decide "the cause has been fixed"; what the checks actually give is that both sets are frozen by exact equality against the log, so a seventh rejection anywhere turns `tests/test_v0_invariants.py:2999` and the new test red, and growing either set requires editing a pinned constant in a commit the principal reviews. State the enforcement in those terms rather than claiming more. (3) The strongest objection, and it must appear: ADR-0043's ACCEPTED decision text says "Refusals already present at the start of the run are counted... and do not block it", which on its face already covers these three, making this ADR unnecessary. It is rejected because "present at the start of the run" is not computable from a snapshot without a stored high-water mark, and a run-relative rule would let ANY corruption self-baseline as soon as the window rolled past it -- A3 would detect nothing. The frozen digest allowlist is the stricter implementation and it stays. (4) The lines are unrecoverable, and note honestly that line 27 is in principle byte-reconstructible -- its `asked` field is provably identical to the `task` of the `dispatch.outcome` at the same timestamp (verified on the intact pair at lines 30/31) -- but splicing it in would rewrite an append-only log, which is worse than the loss. Nothing is repaired; the loss is recorded.

DONE WHEN: `docs/decisions/0105-baseline-the-22-august-capture-loss.md` exists with every template section including "Evidence against"; `python scripts/build_decision_index.py` has regenerated `docs/decisions/index.md` and `tests/test_decision_index.py` is green; and EITHER the principal's decision event is absent and the code half is withheld with that stated, OR it is present, the two-set change and `tests/test_doctor_a3_baseline.py` have landed, `tests/test_v0_invariants.py` is untouched and green, `mypy --strict src/consilient` is clean, and `_capture_condition(Path('.harness/log'))` reports 6 tolerated baseline lines and 0 new. units.title: Make the reviewer receipt arrive, and count every verdict the seam loses
units.commit: fix(driver): make the reviewer receipt arrive and count what is lost
units.note:
MEASURED 24 August 2026. Unit AV built the socket and nothing has ever been plugged into it.

THE DEFECT. `consume_review_verdict` (.harness/build_driver.py:360-427) reads the reviewer's verdict out of `stdout_tail` inside `.harness/dispatch/briefs-driver/<uid>-verify.out` (build_driver.py:373-375, BRIEFS at :32). Of the 49 `*-verify.out` files present: 37 are ZERO BYTES, 10 are raw prose transcripts with no dispatch envelope at all, 1 is `status: refused`, and the ONE file with `status: ok` (A01) ends in prose -- `A01 stays **SOUND**` -- instead of the JSON receipt the brief demands at build_driver.py:951. ZERO of 49 parse. Correspondingly `.harness/log/*.jsonl` holds 44 `review.outcome` events and ALL 44 are `outcome: check_error`, 0 SOUND and 0 DEFECTIVE, all appended within 8 seconds at 16:34 UTC on 24 Aug -- one backfill sweep over absent files, not 44 reviews. `.harness/driver-state.json` reports done: 0, built: 45, review_results: 44 all check_error. Several empty `.out` files have a `.err` ending `...mission denied); it may be held by another process. The trajectory is never partially reported` -- the dispatch refused before the reviewer ever started.

WHY IT MATTERS BEYOND THE PIPELINE. Gate B2 needs the critic's verdicts, and an instrument that returns no observations cannot measure anything. Worse, the loss is plainly non-random -- the long, hard reviews are the ones that hit the leash and the lock -- so the missing rows cannot be assumed ignorable later.

WHAT TO BUILD. Two things, both inside the claimed file.
(a) STOP DEPENDING ON STDOUT. Require the reviewer to write its receipt to `<uid>-verdict.json` and read THAT file. `stdout_tail` is truncated, wrapped differently by different harnesses, and demonstrably invites a model to finish in prose. Update the brief text at build_driver.py:~945-955 to demand the file, and keep the existing strict field/artefact/attempt validation at :378-392 exactly as it is.
(b) MAKE THE LOSS VISIBLE AND TYPED. The single `except ... : pass` at build_driver.py:395-396 collapses six distinct failures into one word. Replace `check_error` with a recorded reason -- at minimum `no_dispatch` (empty or missing .out), `dispatch_refused`, `dispatch_failed`, `no_receipt_file`, `receipt_unparseable`, `receipt_mismatched` (unit/artefact/attempt) -- carried in the `review.outcome` record written at :400-406. This is the accounting the B2 measurement will need for its refusal counts and partial-identification range under ADR-0080 clause 2.

WHAT YOU MUST NOT DO. Do not make an unparseable or missing receipt count as a pass -- fail-closed is the whole of AV and it stays. Do not touch `scripts/dispatch.py`: the trajectory-lock refusal that produced the empty files is unit AU's lock-scope territory, and here it is to be COUNTED as `dispatch_refused`, not fixed. Do not widen the receipt schema, do not accept prose, do not regex for the word SOUND. Do not relax `retired_units` (build_driver.py:343-357).

DONE WHEN. `tests/test_review_verdict.py` gains cases proving a valid receipt file yields SOUND/DEFECTIVE, and that prose output, an absent file, an empty `.out`, a refused dispatch and a mismatched artefact each yield a DISTINCT recorded reason and NONE of them yields SOUND. Plus one end-to-end demonstration on a real dispatched review producing a `review.outcome` event whose outcome is SOUND or DEFECTIVE -- verify by the trajectory event, never by exit code. State in the commit message the classification counts of the 49 historical files you inherited.

units.title: Build the known-bad critic corpus: paired mutant and control artefacts with a snapshot identity
units.commit: feat(exp08): build the paired known-bad critic corpus from EXP-47 mutants
units.note:
Gate B2 needs artefacts whose badness is established INDEPENDENTLY of the critic. Mutation gives that by construction; nothing else available here does. This unit produces the corpus only. It dispatches nothing and computes no beta.

READ FIRST: ADR-0045 (which names mutation as B2's instrument), the EXP-47 entry at docs/10-research/experiment-register.md:1463, and `docs/10-research/experiments/exp47/run_exp47.py`.

THE TRAP, MEASURED. `docs/10-research/experiments/exp47/results-exp47.json` -- the obvious filename -- is an undocumented 22 Aug re-run reporting 13,863 mutants, `pytest_survived: 0`, `equivalent_mutants: 0` and `weakest_guards: []`. It CONTRADICTS the run the register records and yields an EMPTY corpus. The register's live record is the 20 Aug run, in `results-exp47-2026-08-20.json`: 1,931 mutants, 743 pytest survivors, 60 equivalent, 586 non-equivalent COMPOSITE survivors itemised in `weakest_guards` with file, line, operator, orig_snippet and mut_snippet. Use that file, and say in the findings which you used and why. Neither file records a source-snapshot identity and the tree has moved several hundred commits since 20 Aug, so every mutant must be revalidated against the snapshot you actually build on, or regenerated with `run_exp47.py`.

WHY COMPOSITE SURVIVORS AND NOT ALL MUTANTS. The critic only ever reviews artefacts that already went green. A fault pytest catches makes the critic's job trivial and flatters it. The denominator that matters is bad artefacts the composite check ACCEPTS -- which is precisely EXP-47's 586.

WHAT TO BUILD. A deterministic, seeded builder emitting `corpus-exp08.json`. Each item is a PAIR anchored to a real plan unit that already has a commit and whose `claims` include a file under `src/consilient/`:
  - BAD arm: that unit's commit with exactly ONE non-equivalent mutant applied inside a file the unit CLAIMS, committed on a scratch branch so `artefact_identity` (build_driver.py:~330) resolves.
  - CONTROL arm: the same unit's unmutated commit, presented identically.
Pairing controls for unit difficulty and makes a paired analysis available later; it costs nothing here.
Every bad item must be VERIFIED, not assumed: pytest, mypy --strict and ruff all clean at that item's snapshot with the mutation in place (otherwise it is not in the population), and the mutation must be a genuine behavioural change, not an equivalent mutant. Record per item: unit id, base commit, snapshot digest, file, line, operator, orig and mutated snippet, the three check outcomes, and the seed.

SIZING, so the run can be planned. EXP-57 measured a bare model at beta 0.0469 [0.0161, 0.1290] on EXP-47 mutants at n = 64 (register ~line 1636). At that order, 60 bad items give a Wilson half-width near +/-0.06 and 120 near +/-0.04. Emit at least 120 pairs so the run can stage a pilot and still reach the larger n; the run decides how many it spends.

WHAT YOU MUST NOT DO. Do not mutate anything under `tests/` -- EXP-47's registration forbids it and a mutated test measures nothing. Do not hand-pick mutants that look catchable or uncatchable; the sample is seeded and mechanical or it is not a sample. Do not drop an item because a check went red -- record it as excluded with its reason, so the exclusion rate is visible. Do not put the corpus, the manifest or the word `mutant` anywhere a reviewer's brief or worktree can reach; blinding is load-bearing and the run depends on it.

DONE WHEN. `corpus-exp08.json` holds >= 120 verified pairs; `test_build_corpus.py` regenerates the manifest from the seed and asserts it is byte-identical, asserts no bad item fails any of the three checks, asserts no control carries a mutation, and asserts every bad item's mutation lies inside a path its unit claims. Report the exclusion count and reasons in the commit message.

units.title: Run the critic tier over the known-bad corpus and record critic beta with its interval
units.commit: research(exp08): measure critic beta on known-bad artefacts with an interval
units.note:
This is the unit that decides Gate B2. Depends on AX (the receipt must actually arrive -- 0 of 49 do today) and AY (the corpus).

READ FIRST: ADR-0045 in full, ADR-0080 clause 2 (docs/decisions/0080-...md:56-60), the EXP-08 entry at docs/10-research/experiment-register.md:281, and B2's arm at src/consilient/cli.py:506-534.

WHAT TO MEASURE, EXACTLY. beta_critic = P(verdict SOUND | artefact bad by construction), over AY's bad arm. Report alpha = P(verdict DEFECTIVE | artefact is the unmutated control) over the control arm IN THE SAME BREATH: a critic that always says DEFECTIVE has beta 0 and is worthless, and beta alone would reward it. ADR-0045's own 'Evidence against' concedes that a perfectly measured terrible critic satisfies B2; reporting alpha is what stops that being invisible. Wilson 95% intervals on both, computed with `beta.wilson` (src/consilient/beta.py:161) -- do not write a second interval function.

HOW, AND THIS IS THE PART THAT MAKES IT THE TIER RATHER THAN A MODEL. Every item goes through the PRODUCTION seam: the same `<uid>-verify.md` brief the driver writes, the same cross-family rule (reviewer family != authoring family, FAMILY map at build_driver.py:~429), the same family rotation, the same receipt contract AX repaired, consumed by `consume_review_verdict`. The reviewer must not be able to tell it is being measured -- no marker in the brief, no corpus path in the worktree, nothing distinguishing a bad item from a control. If the reviewer can detect the experiment, nothing is measured. EXP-57's number (0.0469 [0.0161, 0.1290], n=64) is a BARE MODEL on a diff and is not this quantity; cite it as sizing context and say plainly that it is not critic-tier beta.

MISSINGNESS IS NOT IGNORABLE, AND MUST NOT BE ASSUMED AWAY. Today's yield is 0 of 49, and the losses correlate with review difficulty. Run a 10-item PILOT first and report the receipt yield before spending the rest. Every non-receipt is counted, never dropped: report the refusal/error/timeout counts by AX's typed reason and the PARTIAL-IDENTIFICATION RANGE that ADR-0080 clause 2 requires -- beta_low = accepts / all bad items, beta_high = (accepts + non-receipts) / all bad items. A point estimate that silently conditions on the receipt arriving is the sampling defect beta.py:14-22 already documents, one level out.

TYPE THE ROWS. Every result row carries `estimand_kind: "critic_proxy_beta"`, its frozen verifier contract (brief version, receipt schema, family pairing), sample and coverage counts, and the refusal breakdown -- ADR-0080 clause 2. It is a Tier 2 quantity, and Tier 2 is exactly what B2 asks for.

WHAT YOU MUST NOT DO -- read this twice.
- Do NOT touch `PROXY_ESTIMAND_KINDS` (beta.py:41), `admits_human_beta_row` (beta.py:186) or `admits_sizing_input`. `critic_proxy_beta` stays REFUSED by the human-beta projection; that exclusion is what makes it admissible here. tests/test_verdict_supply.py:135,153 enforces it and must stay green untouched.
- Do NOT touch `src/consilient/cli.py`. B2's arm already works and is already tested (tests/test_v0_invariants.py:2498, :2513, :2887). Note for the record, do not fix: cli.py:526-534 passes B2 on `low <= point <= high` with no half-width bound, unlike A1's <=0.05 at cli.py:472, so `0.5 [0.0, 1.0]` would pass. Tightening that is a gate change reserved to the principal under ADR-0039. Your obligation is to REPORT the half-width in the register entry and the findings so he can decide -- not to exploit the gap, and not to close it.
- Do NOT tune the corpus, drop items, re-run arms or re-seed to move the number. If the pilot yield is poor, or the corpus fails revalidation, or the measurement is too wide to be worth anything, the honest outcome is that B2 stays FAIL and you say why. A finding that the instrument is not ready is worth more than a number that is not.

THE REGISTER EDIT, AND THE ONE THING TO ASK ABOUT. `docs/10-research/experiment-register.md` is the evidence base and AGENTS.md marks changing it ASK FIRST. Get the principal's acknowledgement before committing that file. EXP-08's current registration -- 'run a local 14B as a diff critic over historical PRs with known outcomes', with a stopping rule about ADR-0007's parallelism ceiling -- is NOT the mutation route ADR-0045 mandates. Preserve it VERBATIM under a `#### Pre-registration (preserved; do not re-allocate EXP-08)` heading, exactly as EXP-57 does at experiment-register.md ~line 1680, and add the new registration above it with its own pre-registered stopping rules. Say explicitly whether the old ceiling stopping rule is carried across or retired, and why. A re-registration that quietly drops a stopping rule is the failure ADR-0045 was written about.

DONE WHEN. EXP-08's heading reads DONE with a date and a findings reference; its entry contains `critic-beta-measured: p [lo, hi]` matching cli.py:99 with the half-width stated beside it; `findings-exp08.md` reports beta, alpha, n per arm, the refusal breakdown, the partial-identification range, the blinding measures taken and what the measurement cannot decide; and `consil doctor --json` is run and its B2 reason quoted literally in the commit message -- whatever it says. Verify by that output, not by exit code.

condition: B4 — "Twenty non-Consilient tickets complete without harness intervention" (`src/consilient/cli.py:175`; `docs/40-spec/v0-draft.md:154` words it "without intervention in the harness itself"). units.title: Make _foreign_tickets refuse rows that carry no re-derivable evidence, and delete its false append() claim
units.commit: fix(b4): admit only foreign tickets whose row can be re-derived
units.note:
THE DEFECT. `src/consilient/cli.py:791-792` states: "Counted over `append()`-validated events only. A ticket recorded by writing to the file directly does not count, because nothing checked it." That is false. `events.read()` (events.py:2787) classifies lines through `_classify_lines`, which calls the same `validate()` that `append()` calls; `append()` (events.py:2732-2748) adds only an auto `event_id` — optional in `validate()` — and a transition validator, and only `CANDIDATE_EXPOSED_KIND` and `VERIFICATION_OUTCOME_KIND` are registered (events.py:3581-3585). Neither `attempt.outcome` nor `ticket.completed` is governed.

EVIDENCE [measured] 24 Aug 2026: 40 lines typed by hand into one `.jsonl`, never through `append()`, actor `a.human.with.a.text.editor`, each pair being an `attempt.outcome` with `verifier_accept: true` plus a `ticket.completed`, repository `pytest-dev/pytest` — `_foreign_tickets` returned 20. A text editor opens Gate B4.

WHAT TO DO. Tighten `_foreign_tickets` (cli.py:788-833) so an `attempt.outcome` only enters `verified_attempts` when, in addition to today's conditions, its `data` carries all three of: `harness` (non-empty string naming the runtime that did the work), `corpus_revision` (non-empty string), and `receipt_sha256` (64 lowercase hex, matching `[0-9a-f]{64}`). Reject the row otherwise — silently, as today, by not adding it. Then REPLACE the false docstring paragraph with the true one: this counter checks SHAPE and cannot check truth; what it enforces is that every counted row carries the three things a third party needs to re-run the ticket and compare. Say that limit out loud rather than implying a protection.

WHAT MUST NOT BE DONE. Do not touch `B4_TICKETS_REQUIRED` (cli.py:82), `THIS_REPOSITORIES` (cli.py:83), the gate text (cli.py:175) or any ADR status — those are the principal's. Do not add a fourth field because it seems tidy; three is what re-derivation needs. Do not weaken any existing condition: `verifier_accept is True or == 1`, the non-empty `data.ticket` requirement and the distinct-pair dedupe all stay. Do not backfill, rewrite or hand-edit any line in `.harness/log/` — the trajectory is append-only. Do not claim the tightening makes the log unforgeable; a writer can always compute what a check computes, and the docstring must say so.

DONE WHEN. A new `tests/test_foreign_ticket_admission.py` proves, without touching `tests/test_b4_tickets.py`: (1) hand-written rows carrying all three new fields still count — shape, not provenance, is what this checks; (2) a row missing `harness`, missing `corpus_revision`, or carrying a `receipt_sha256` that is not 64 lowercase hex is NOT counted, one case each; (3) the live `.harness/log` still yields 0 (measured today: 0, so no regression is possible here). `mypy --strict` on `src/consilient/cli.py` is clean before you claim it works. Report the count `consil doctor` gives for B4 after the change; if it moved, say why.

units.title: Replace b4_tickets.py's mutation-revert rule with one that can express real upstream change
units.commit: fix(b4): credit bounded real repairs, not byte-identical restorations
deps: Make _foreign_tickets refuse rows that carry no re-derivable evidence, and delete its false append() claim
units.note:
THE DEFECT. `scripts/b4_tickets.py:261` snapshots `original = manifest(isolated)` before seeding and `:299` refuses credit unless `manifest(isolated) == original`. The only creditable outcome is a tree byte-identical to the pin, so every ticket the script can express is a synthetic mutation revert: `_seed` writes `ticket.after`, the agent restores `ticket.before`, net diff zero. Unit AP's own brief required work sourced from pytest's own open issues and defensible to a maintainer; this rule makes that impossible to record. Confirmed by the passing test at `tests/test_b4_tickets.py:261-273`, whose "agent" is a `python -c` that does `read_bytes().replace(after, before)` — the suite proves the plumbing, never an agent.

SECOND DEFECT, same file. `_credit` (:207-239) writes no harness identity, and `--agent-argv` (:339) is `nargs=REMAINDER` and accepts any argv, so the credited row cannot tell a harness completing work unaided — the literal gate condition — from a shell one-liner. `docs/40-spec/v0-draft.md:171` requires every contribution record to identify runtime/session identity, execution harness, provider and model. THIRD: receipts go into a `TemporaryDirectory` (:256) that is deleted on exit, so no B4 run leaves any retained artefact.

WHAT TO DO. (a) Replace the restoration rule with a bounded-change rule: the target test must go red then green, the upstream suite (`FULL_SUITE`, and whatever suite the ticket's own area names) must stay green, the diff must be CONFINED to paths the ticket declares, and `manifest(isolated) != original` must now be REQUIRED — a no-op is not a ticket and must not credit. (b) Retain receipts: write them to a durable directory keyed by ticket id under `.harness/` (instance data, gitignored — never tracked, never published), and record `receipt_sha256` as the SHA-256 over the concatenated receipt files in a fixed order. (c) Add the three fields unit B4-A now requires to the `attempt.outcome` in `_credit`: `harness` (taken from the resolved agent argv, not free text), `corpus_revision` (the value `_read_commit_id` already derives, :134-146), `receipt_sha256`. (d) Retire the synthetic `TICKETS` tuple (:56-89) — replace it with tickets loaded from the pool unit B4-C produces. If that pool is not yet available, land (a)–(c) with the seeded tickets marked explicitly in the source as SYNTHETIC and make `_credit` refuse to write a `ticket.completed` for a synthetic one, so the runner cannot credit anything until real tickets exist.

WHAT MUST NOT BE DONE. Do not open a pull request, do not push a branch, do not comment on any upstream issue — producing the verified work is this unit; submitting anything is the principal's decision alone. Do not touch anything under `.harness/log/`. Do not relax the red-phase guard (`red != 1` at :272 — exit 2 is a collection error, not a red test; the test at tests/test_b4_tickets.py:140 pins this). Do not widen `THIS_REPOSITORIES` or edit `src/consilient/cli.py` — B4-A owns that file. Do not invent tickets to reach a number.

DONE WHEN. `tests/test_b4_tickets.py` proves: a repair that changes nothing does NOT credit; a repair that changes a path the ticket did not declare does NOT credit; a bounded real repair DOES credit and `_foreign_tickets` counts it under the tightened rule; and the receipt directory survives the run with a digest matching the recorded `receipt_sha256`. Use the corpus venv interpreter `C:/Users/jpbpr/Repositories/pytest-upstream/.venv/Scripts/python.exe` for all corpus work — the system interpreter resolves a different pytest and the import error is confusing. Report the B4 count from `consil doctor`; 0 is the correct and expected answer until real tickets land.

units.title: Count how many pytest open issues are actually admissible as B4 tickets, and report the number
units.commit: feat(b4): enumerate the admissible upstream ticket pool from public issues
units.note:
THE QUESTION. Nobody has counted how much real, defensible upstream work exists, and B4 needs twenty. Guessing is the failure mode this project is named after. [measured] 24 Aug 2026 via the GitHub API: pytest-dev/pytest carries 114 open `type: bug` issues, so the raw pool is not the constraint. [measured] the same day: pytest's own issue-referencing xfail/skip register in `testing/` holds only 5 markers for #10042, one `skipif` for #13896 and one `skip` for #13485 — roughly 3 distinct maintainer-declared defects with a built-in red phase. So the two obvious routes bracket the answer between 3 and 114 and nothing narrows it. Narrow it.

WHAT TO DO. Write `scripts/b4_pool.py`: sweep pytest-dev/pytest open issues through the PUBLIC GitHub API (no credential — this is public read; if a token would be needed, do not use one and say so, per the no-secrets rule), and classify each against a stated ADMISSION RULE that you write down in the module docstring before you run it. The rule must be about whether the RED PHASE COMES FROM UPSTREAM, not from us: an issue is admissible only if it carries a reproducer — a runnable snippet, a stated failing invocation, or a matching `xfail`/`skip`/`skipif` in `testing/` naming its number — from which a failing test can be written without inventing what "correct" means. Inventing the oracle is exactly the beta failure this project measures, so an issue with no upstream-stated expected behaviour is INADMISSIBLE and must be recorded as such with its reason. Record per issue: number, title, URL, labels, created date, retrieval date, admissible yes/no, and the reason. Write the result to `.harness/b4-pool.json` (instance data, gitignored, never tracked or published) and PRINT THE THREE COUNTS: swept, admissible, inadmissible-with-reason-breakdown.

Repeat the same sweep for at least one further permissively-licensed public repository this project actually depends on, and record its licence and retrieval date. Twenty tickets on one repository is one class of facts — one suite, one set of conventions; tickets across independently-authored suites is a genuinely different class, which is the CONSILIENCE.md reason to spread them, not merely a way to reduce load on one maintainer team.

WHAT MUST NOT BE DONE. Do not open issues, do not comment, do not open pull requests, do not touch any upstream repository — this unit only READS public data. Do not write to `docs/10-research/` (changing the evidence base is ask-first). Do not touch `src/consilient/cli.py`, `scripts/b4_tickets.py` or `tests/` — other units own those. Do not pad the admissible list to reach seventeen: if the admissible count is under seventeen, that is the finding and it belongs to the principal.

DONE WHEN. The script runs, the three counts are printed, and you report them plainly with the admission rule you used quoted verbatim. State whether seventeen further admissible tickets exist. If they do not, say so — that is a fact about Gate B4 worth more than any workaround, and the principal decides what follows. Leave one runnable self-check (an `assert`-based `__main__` or a small test) that the classifier rejects an issue with no reproducer, so the rule cannot silently soften later.
